flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e4 leaves your pawn hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been moving your e7-bishop to f6 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: I opened the g3–c7 diagonal and hung my queen. You talked about a pawn. Qg3 was staring through e5 at Qc7 — that discovered hit is the 239-centipawn lesson, not 'your pawn hanging.' Bf6 isn't 'saving a pawn'; it keeps the lid on that diagonal so the queen doesn't drop.

flags.quote: Taking the queen on c7 with your queen puts it at risk of attack from the black king. A better move would have been moving your d2-bishop to f4 because you can likely take a queen.
flags.critique: I traded a protected queen and you described the recapture like I hung my own queen. Bf4 adds a second attacker on c7: two attackers, the king defends once, I win the queen for a bishop. 'Likely take a queen' is weasel copy when the double attack is forced. Teach two-on-one, not 'puts it at risk.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on h7 with your d3-bishop is a mistake because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the black g8-rook.
flags.critique: You called it a mistake because the pawn was free. That's why I'd take it, not why I shouldn't. h7 does not defend the rook on g8 — pawns don't protect straight ahead. The real story is my king is still in the center and the bishop can get trapped on h7. Don't glue capture-brag reasons onto a mistake verdict.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your queen is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook and then pin another pawn to the queen.
flags.critique: I recaptured a pawn. You invented a pin combo — g7 to a rook, d7 to a queen, 'and then' — like I played a tactic sequence. Those pins are geometric trivia. Teach: you take the pawn back with the queen, and Black will kick it with ...Nc6.

flags.quote: Moving your b8-knight to c6 is the strongest move because you control more central squares.
flags.critique: The knight attacks the queen on d4. That's why this move exists in every 2.d4 Sicilian with Qxd4. 'Control more central squares' is the same cardboard as e4/c5. I needed 'kick the queen.'

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to d5 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your f6-knight to g4 because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: Nd5 does not create a backward pawn. My knight was kicked by e5 and I parked it in the center hitting the queen. Ng4 is better because it hits the queen and the e5 pawn (and f2) — a fork, not 'likely take a pawn.' You picked pawn structure as the problem while the tactics sat in the reason list unused.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g5 is a blunder, but moving your e7-bishop to f6 would be better.
flags.critique: I kicked the knight and it jumped into Nd5+, forking my king and bishop. You said 'blunder, Bf6 would be better' with zero why. That's the whole lesson: don't chase a piece into a check-fork. A 280-centipawn collapse with a blank because-clause is just a red sticker.

flags.quote: Moving your c1-bishop to g5 is a blunder, but moving your knight to e2 would be better.
flags.critique: 223 centipawns, no reason. After Bg5, ...Bb4+ is a pain and my king is stuck in the center. 'Ne2 would be better' without saying it develops toward castling. If you can't name why the blunder loses, don't bother labeling it.

flags.quote: Moving your d6-bishop to e7 is the strongest move because it saves your e7-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: It wasn't an e7-bishop until I put it there. c5 was eating the bishop on d6. 'Saves your e7-bishop from capture' is a destination-square tautology. Say it retreats the bishop from c5.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: d4 hits the queen on e3. Strongest move, empty reasons. I noticed the queen was hanging. You didn't. Same hole as Nc6: attacking the queen lost to a blank verdict.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: f5 hits the queen on g3. If a pawn attacks a queen, that is the sentence. 'Ignored threat' in the reason list never made it to English. Third time this game you missed a queen-hit.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: c5 attacks the bishop I just parked on d6. Tempo, hanging piece, the whole point of the pawn push. You gave me a period. I already know I moved a pawn to c5.

flags.quote: Moving your g8-rook to h8 is the strongest move because it saves your h8-rook from capture.
flags.critique: Destination-square again: it wasn't an h8-rook until I moved it. Bxh7 was attacking the rook, yes, but Rh8 also hits the bishop that just took on h7. You taught a tautology and skipped the trap.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is a mistake, but moving your g1-knight to f3 would be better.
flags.critique: The because on the played move is center_control — the same praise you gave e4. e5 is premature: it kicks the knight onto a better square and I still haven't developed the kingside. Nf3 needs a why (develop, castle, stop ...Ng4), not a silent 'would be better.'

flags.quote: Moving your h7-bishop to c2 is the strongest move because it saves your c2-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Third retreat this game named by the landing square. The bishop ran away from the rook on h8. 'Retreats the bishop from h7' is English. 'Saves your c2-bishop' sounds like a different piece.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to b4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: I just castled queenside. b4 starts a pawn storm at my king. That is the plan. Empty 'strongest move' treats a king attack like a random pawn shove.

flags.quote: Moving your c8-bishop to d7 is a mistake, but moving your queen to d5 would be better because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: Which pawn? Which rook? Bd7 is developing toward castling; the 165-centipawn miss is a queen centralization I can't picture from that clause. Empty reasons on the move I played, and a pin I can't find.

flags.quote: Moving your f8-bishop to d6 leaves your pawn hanging to the white d3-bishop. A better move would have been moving your pawn to g5.
flags.critique: You already told me that pawn (h7, name it) was hanging on Rg8. I still didn't save it, and Bd6 also steps onto the c-pawn's path. Same hanging-pawn sentence twice, never say h7, never mention the bishop walking into c5.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e7 with your knight is the strongest move because you take the defender of the black pawn.
flags.critique: I completed the fork and won a bishop. You said I took the defender of a pawn — which pawn? Lead with winning the piece. 'Removed defender of a pawn' undersells a free bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f6 is a mistake, but moving your f8-bishop to b4 would be better because it forces the king to respond.
flags.critique: f6 kicks the bishop and weakens my king. Your reasons include king_safer — backwards. Bb4+ is check, not a vague 'forces the king to respond.' Tell me I missed a check and pushed a weakening pawn instead.

flags.quote: Moving your c2-bishop to b1 is a mistake, but moving your c2-bishop to b3 would be better.
flags.critique: The d3 pawn is attacking the bishop on c2. I tucked it to b1. You said 'Bb3 would be better' with no why — 179 centipawns of silence. At least say Bb3 keeps the bishop active on a useful diagonal instead of burying it on b1.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is a blunder, but taking the pawn on g5 with your d2-bishop would be better because you pin the knight to the rook and the pawn was undefended.
flags.critique: Bxg5 is actually a decent better-move line. The played move gets no problem sentence for a 475-centipawn collapse. I ignored a hanging pawn plus a pin and maybe opened my king. 'Is a blunder, take g5 instead' still doesn't tell me what f3 did wrong.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: That's the e4 sentence with a different square. This is 2.d4 in the Sicilian — I'm opening the d-file to recapture with the queen, not repeating a center slogan. Three plies, one idea, I'm already skimming.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reasons. e6 is the structure move — blunts the e-file, prepares ...Be7 or ...d5. After a row of 'That's the one,' a blank strongest-move is wallpaper. If you detected nothing, don't pretend there's a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d3 leaves your pawn hanging to the white d2-bishop. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e3.
flags.critique: 493 centipawns. You named the hanging d3 pawn, then suggested e3 with no idea. Is e3 a protected passer? Does it jam the bishops? A five-pawn swing needs more than a SAN.

suggestions.title: Never use capture virtues as the because of a mistake
suggestions.detail: On Bxh7 the verdict is 'mistake' while playedBecause is wins_material plus removed_defender — 'because the pawn was undefended.' In select-insight / templates, if classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, drop capture/wins_material/removed_defender from playedBecause and require a problem reason (hanging, king still central, trapped). A 1200 hears 'it's bad because you won a pawn' and stops trusting the coach.

suggestions.title: Prefer the highest-value hanging piece, including discovered queens
suggestions.detail: ...e4 hung Qc7 on the opened g3–c7 diagonal; copy talked about a pawn (ignored_threat on e5). When ranking hanging/ignored_threat, sort by piece value and treat discovered attacks that unveil a queen hit as first-class facts in move-effects. Suggested-move 'saves a pawn' must not outrank 'your queen is en prise.' This is the difference between teaching a tactic and inventing a pawn story.

suggestions.title: Name retreated pieces by the square they left
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses ownedPhrase on the piece after the move, so Be7 'saves your e7-bishop,' Rh8 'saves your h8-rook,' Bc2 'saves your c2-bishop.' Label from the origin square, or render 'it retreats the bishop from d6 / h7.' Three tautologies in one game is a template farm, not coaching.

suggestions.title: If the move attacks the queen, that is the because
suggestions.detail: Nc6 vs Qd4, ...d4 vs Qe3, ...f5 vs Qg3, c5 vs Bd6 all came out as center_control, empty strongest-move, or development. Add an 'attacks_piece' fact (or promote existing attacks on Q/K) and let pickBenefitReasons rank it above center_control/development. A 1200 already knows knights go to c6; they need 'it kicks the queen.'

suggestions.title: Don't lead recaptures with incidental pawn pins
suggestions.detail: Qxd4 selected pin+pin over wins_material and emitted 'pin the pawn to the rook and then pin another pawn to the queen.' For recaptures of a hanging unit, prefer capture/wins_material. Demote relative pins of pawns unless the pin is the tactical point (absolute pin, or the pinned unit is a piece). selectBecauseReasons already prefers tactics — it needs a 'incidental pawn pin' filter so 'then' doesn't invent a sequence.

suggestions.title: Refuse blank copy on mistakes and blunders
suggestions.detail: Bg5, g5, Bd7, Bb1, f3, e5 all nudge with 'would be better' and no played problem, or no suggested because. If shouldNudge and both because slots are empty, fall back to suggested-move effects (check, develop-toward-castle, fork) or a generic 'this hangs into a tactic — compare with X' rather than a naked SAN. Empty blunder labels train the learner to ignore the mascot.

suggestions.title: Say 'you win the queen' when SEE is forced
suggestions.detail: describeReason uses 'you can likely take' whenever capture.likely is set, so Bf4 vs Qc7 and Ng4 vs e5 sound speculative. If SEE (or two-attackers vs one-defender) is clearly winning, use the non-likely branch: 'you win the queen' / 'you take the pawn after the queen moves.' 'Likely' is how a 1200 hears 'the engine is guessing.'

suggestions.title: Don't headline backward pawns when a fork is the story
suggestions.detail: Nd5 picked problem_backward_pawn while fork/outpost/saves_piece sat unused, and Ng4's because collapsed to 'likely take a pawn.' pickProblemReasons should not choose doubled/backward/isolated when a hanging piece, check, or fork exists on the suggested line. Pawn-structure phrases are fine in quiet positions; they are wrong chess on a queen-attacking knight jump.

whatWorked: ...d6 actually taught the discovered bishop hit on Qh3 — rare concrete tactic copy.
Qe3 said the queen was hanging; Nd5+ named the king-and-bishop fork.
Rg8 correctly flagged h7 hanging to Bd3; Rxd3 named the pin of bishop to rook plus the free pawn.
Bf5 stacked skewer (rook to b1-bishop) and discovered rook attack without sounding fake.
Castle copy on ...O-O-O (and the O-O suggestion on a3) is the one phrase-bank line that teaches a plan.
